pgvector is an open-source extension for PostgreSQL, the widely used relational database. It lets a team store "embeddings," which are numerical representations of text, images, or other content that capture meaning, and then quickly find items that are similar in meaning. This powers features such as semantic search (finding results by intent rather than exact keywords), product or content recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation, where an AI assistant pulls relevant company data before answering. Its main business advantage is that it works inside the existing Postgres database, so teams avoid adopting, paying for, and synchronizing a separate specialized vector database. The trade-off is scale: for very large datasets or demanding real-time workloads, dedicated vector stores may offer better performance, so product teams should benchmark against their expected volume.
